restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; fresh independent uniform 256-bit words, not seeded PRNG expansion.
Exactly 32-byte messages msg(x)=LE32(x), one 136-byte rate block m||0x06||zeros||0x80; complete SHA3-256 sponge with all-zero state, prefix Keccak rounds 0 through 4, and all 256 digest bits.
Single-processor van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point search with theta=2^-32, chain cap L=2^40, budget K0=65162*2^112 evaluations and record cap 2^98; one finite run, no restarts.
One finite run with at most 2^128.02 target-compression equivalents of total charged computation and at most 2^112 peak bytes; no nonuniform advice or precomputed collision.
Analytic resource and success bounds under score-critical heuristic H-RF; no full-scale execution, cryptanalytic weakness or nominal-reference improvement is claimed.

heuristics.statement: Each evaluation of the 5-round SHA3-256 ordinary-collision map f at a fresh input returns a value uniform on {0,1}^256, independent of all previous coins and outputs.
heuristics.scope: Used only for the success-probability bound of the distinguished-point walk (first-contact and bad-event estimates). Correctness and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds hold for every run without this premise.
heuristics.extrapolation: From standard generic-search modeling to the fixed 5-round prefix sponge; no differential, independence-across-rounds or balance premise about Keccak structure is assumed beyond generic random-function behavior for contact statistics.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is a modeling heuristic, not a proved property of the fixed function. Supporting discussion is analytic (birthday contact arithmetic plus standard DP literature); no organizer-executed scaled experiment is declared. The claimed margin above 0.39 is about 8.0e-06 before deducting bad events below 7.0e-10.
